title: Understanding Singular Value Decomposition
text: When performing Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) on a matrix, the diagonal matrix \(S\) contains the singular values of the matrix \(X\). These singular values are related to the eigenvalues of \(X**TX\). What can you infer about the singular values if the rank of \(X\) is less than \(d\)?

title: Rank and Singular Values
text: The rank of a matrix is the number of non-zero singular values it has. If \(rank(X)<d\), what does this tell you about the number of non-zero singular values in \(S\)?

title: Analyzing the Diagonal of \(S\)
text: Given that \(rank(X)<d\), which of the following must be true about the diagonal of \(S\)?
choices: All values on the diagonal of S are $$non-zero$$.
The diagonal of S is irrelevant to the rank of X.
There must be at least one $$0$$ along the diagonal of S.
